headline: Revenue dips on divestiture comp, ARR beats, guidance raised
summary_short: PTC's fiscal Q3'26 (quarter ended June 30, 2026, tracked here as FY2026 Q2) revenue fell 7% y/y to $600M and GAAP diluted EPS fell 12% to $1.03, both hit by the March 2026 Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture, while as-reported ARR excluding divested businesses rose 7% to $2,412M, beating the high end of guidance.
summary_long: Revenue fell 7% y/y to $600M and GAAP diluted EPS fell 12% to $1.03, mainly reflecting the March 2026 Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture rather than organic softness; non-GAAP EPS fell 4% to $1.58. GAAP operating margin contracted 480bps to 28% (non-GAAP -290bps to 41%) as revenue fell against a similar cost base. ARR excluding divested businesses rose 7% y/y to $2,412M (9.1% constant-currency), above the high end of guidance; operating cash flow (+7% to $261M) and free cash flow (+3% to $249M) also beat guidance. PTC raised FY2026 revenue, ARR and EPS guidance and reaffirmed cash-flow guidance, and repurchased $525M of stock, partly funded by $225M of new borrowing; cash rose to $351M and long-term debt rose to $1,398M.

drivers.explanation: Driven by the March 13, 2026 divestiture of the Kepware and ThingWorx businesses, which removed their revenue from the prior-year comp base; the release states revenue declined 8% y/y on a constant-currency basis.
Flows from the same divestiture-driven revenue decline; the release's footnote states revenue, operating margin and EPS are all impacted under ASC 606 for this reason.
Tracks the diluted EPS decline; basic (114.68M) and diluted (114.98M) weighted-average shares are nearly identical this quarter, so the two metrics move together.
Declines less than GAAP EPS because non-GAAP excludes stock-based compensation, acquired-intangible amortization, and acquisition/transaction charges per the release's own reconciliation table.
Reflects the divestiture-driven revenue and operating-income decline, partly offset by a smaller net other-expense of $14.1M versus $16.2M a year ago.
Revenue fell 7% while total operating expenses were nearly flat ($324.0M vs $324.1M), so the decline flows almost entirely from the top line.
Arithmetic result of a 7% revenue decline against a flat total-operating-expense base; not separately narrated in the release beyond the ASC 606/divestiture footnote already cited for revenue.
Smaller compression than the GAAP margin because non-GAAP operating income excludes stock-based compensation and acquired-intangible amortization from both periods.

The release states ARR was flat y/y on an as-reported basis including divested businesses, but grew 7% (9.1% constant-currency) when Kepware/ThingWorx ARR is excluded from the year-ago base, beating the high end of guidance.
Not broken out by cause beyond the CEO/CFO's general characterization of 'strong execution' this quarter (see overall driver); exceeded the high end of guidance.
Operating cash flow growth outpaced a rise in capital expenditures ($11.3M this quarter vs $1.9M a year ago), so FCF still grew despite higher capex.
Reflects $523.3M of divestiture proceeds received earlier in FY26 and $225M of new borrowing this quarter, partly offset by $1,326.2M of YTD share repurchases, per the cash-flow statement.
The cash-flow statement shows $225M of net new borrowings in the quarter; the release does not narrate the purpose beyond the borrowings line itself.
Explicitly raised and narrowed from the previous $2,580M-$2,820M range per the release's headline bullet 'Raising FY26 guidance for ARR, Revenue and EPS.'
Explicitly raised from the previous $7.21-$9.70 range per the same headline guidance bullet, reflecting year-to-date outperformance versus plan.

CEO Neil Barua cited strong Q3 execution and growing customer interest in AI atop PTC's Intelligent Product Lifecycle vision; CFO Jen DiRico cited a 'compressed valuation' of PTC stock as the reason for repurchasing more than double the quarter's original buyback target.
